claim.claim: Microsoft's gross margin percentage declined in the quarter ended December 31, 2025 because of the costs of scaling its AI infrastructure.

verdict.label: SUPPORTED

supporting_evidence.quote: Gross margin percentage decreased slightly driven by continued investments in AI infrastructure and growing AI product usage, offset in part by efficiency gains across the Microsoft Cloud and sales mix shift to higher margin businesses.

Gross margin percentage decreased slightly driven by continued investments in AI infrastructure and growing AI product usage, offset in part by efficiency gains across the Microsoft Cloud and sales mix shift to higher margin businesses.

verdict.reasoning_summary:
The claim makes both a numeric assertion (that gross margin percentage declined) and an interpretive assertion (that the decline was because of AI infrastructure costs). 

For the quarter ended December 31, 2025, evidence E2 and E5 both explicitly state that "Gross margin percentage decreased slightly driven by continued investments in AI infrastructure and growing AI product usage." This directly supports both the numeric fact of the decline and the stated cause.

The evidence uses the phrase "investments in AI infrastructure" which aligns with the claim's reference to "costs of scaling its AI infrastructure." Both E2 and E5 are from the 10-Q filed 2026-01-28 for the period ended 2025-12-31, which is exactly the quarter in question.

The claim is fully supported by the evidence.
